Dietary Supplements offers information on dietary supple-
ments via its website and its My Dietary Supplements (MYDS) 
mobile application. The Nutrient Data System for Research 
from the University of Minnesota provides ongoing updates for 
generic and branded products, as well as a dietary supplement 
assessment module. The ProNutra database, from VioCare, 
Inc., is designed for research diets controlled in many nutrients. 
It includes customizable calculation algorithms, with research 
kitchen outputs (Viocare, 2009).
Food and nutrition management software systems such 
as Computrition or CBORD are designed for institutional 
use and typically include extensive nutrient databases. 
These systems may regularly import data from the SR. Other 
food database software programs designed and priced for 
individual use are available; however, their cost and their 
comprehensiveness vary. Only certain software programs 
are approved for use in the USDA School Meals program 
(Stein, 2011).
